Prose context only — this section states that acceptance criteria were derived from assumptions rather than team consultation; it names no testable behavior, route, or status code.

Cross-cutting guarantee, not a distinct testable behavior. Its assertion is a disjunctive status range (200 or any 4xx), which the case DSL cannot express — 'expect.status' admits only a single exact integer and there is no range/anyOf matcher for status. The concrete instances of this guarantee are enumerated and compiled elsewhere in the intent (sections 1.3-1.6, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.6, 4.3); compiling this section would duplicate that coverage while weakening the assertions.

Prose requirement statement only — a quality-attribute goal ('execution of any request should not cause a service interruption') with no concrete route, payload, or response behavior to assert. It names no acceptance criterion of its own; the automatable robustness criteria live in the numbered 4.x section, and the service-interruption property itself is a load/stress concern the intent explicitly defers to other tooling (4.10, 4.11).

Prose context only — this section enumerates quality attributes that motivate the acceptance criteria elsewhere in the document; it states no testable behavior of its own and names the criteria sections (Security, API guarantees, Robustness, Parallel execution) that cover it.

Umbrella prose criteria, not distinct behaviors: 'never any status code other than 200 or 4xx' is a blanket property over all requests rather than a specific request/response pair, and 'behave according to the API specifications' is context restating the spec. Both are realized by the concrete, automatable criteria in the POST /groovy/submit (2.1-2.4), GET /groovy/status (3.1-3.6), Security (1.1-1.6), and Robustness (4.x) sections, which pin exact routes, payloads, and status codes.

5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 each name their own coverage elsewhere (the general automation suite, 4.5, and 4.5-4.8), so compiling them here would duplicate. 5.3 asserts a concurrency bound — that at most two submissions are IN_PROGRESS at any instant — which is a cross-request property observed at a single moment in time; the case DSL expresses one test request with one subset assertion and forbids wall-clock waiting, so the two-at-a-time capacity limit cannot be observed without racing or timing. No automatable functional API case remains for this section.
